sections.h2: Which Washington, NJ is this, and what should a seller know?
sections.html:
New Jersey has five municipalities named Washington Township, plus Washington Borough in Warren County. This page covers Washington Township in Gloucester County, the South Jersey community of Sewell, Turnersville and Grenloch with about 49,840 residents. If your house is in that township, three things drive a fast sale: the township's resale certificate, the state's seller fees, and the Gloucester County assessment calendar.

You can list with an agent, sell privately, or accept a cash offer for the house as it stands. Each route runs through the same township and state steps below.

sections.h2: Where is Washington Township and how did it grow?
sections.html:
The township covers 21.35 square miles of land in northern Gloucester County and borders Deptford, Mantua, Monroe, Glassboro, Pitman and Gloucester Township. The legislature incorporated it in 1836 out of Deptford Township. It belonged to Camden County from 1844 until 1871, when most of it returned to Gloucester County.

The oldest community, Grenloch Terrace, began as a Lenape settlement called Tetamekon. Turnersville is named for the Turner family, Hurffville for the Hurff family and Sewell for General William Joyce Sewell. Census counts moved from 47,114 in 2000 to 48,559 in 2010 and 48,677 in 2020, with a July 1, 2025 estimate of 49,840, which shows steady, modest growth.

Two centers anchor local business. One is the town center around Greentree Road, Egg Harbor Road, Ganttown Road and Hurffville-Crosskeys Road, near Washington Township High School and Washington Lake Park. The other follows Route 42, which links Philadelphia to the Jersey Shore.

sections.h2: How do the roads and transit around Washington Township affect buyers?
sections.html:
Route 42 (Black Horse Pike) runs along the east side, Route 47 (Delsea Drive) along the west, and the Atlantic City Expressway ends at Route 42 inside the township. Route 55 clips the eastern tip, and county roads 534 and 555 feed local traffic. Of the 199.78 miles of public road, 154.61 miles belong to the township, so most streets are maintained by the municipality.

  • PATCO Speedline and the NJ Transit Atlantic City line are at Lindenwold, about 10 miles northeast.
  • NJ Transit buses 315, 400, 403, 408 and 412 run to Philadelphia, and route 463 serves local stops.

sections.h2: What do Census figures show about Washington Township homes?
sections.html:
Washington Township is mainly a place of owners. The Census Bureau puts the owner-occupied rate at 83.1% for 2020 to 2024, the median owner-occupied home value at $337,600, median owner costs at $2,437 a month with a mortgage and $1,153 without, and median household income at $114,249. There are 18,444 households averaging 2.65 people.

That median value sits just under $350,000, the line where the state Realty Transfer Fee schedule changes. A sale at or below that price uses a lower rate table than a sale above it, so the contract price decides which table applies. Ask your closing attorney to run both numbers before you accept an offer.

The Census Bureau also reports that 18.3% of residents are 65 or older, 21.7% are under 18, 91.7% lived in the same house a year earlier, and workers average a 29.4-minute commute. Veterans number 2,385. Long-tenured owners and commuting families are the two groups most likely to be buying or selling here.

sections.h2: What does the township Housing office require for a sale?
sections.html:
The Housing office at the Washington Township municipal building, 523 Egg Harbor Road in Sewell, runs certificate of occupancy inspections so buyers and tenants move into a safe property. Its page lists a Certificate of Resale Application and an inspection checklist. The office phone is 856-589-0520.

Get the current application, fee and inspection timing from that office before you sign a contract, and have repairs finished before the inspector arrives. A failed item can delay settlement, so fix the obvious ones, such as smoke alarms, handrails and missing permits.

  • New Jersey requires 10-year sealed-battery smoke alarms in one- and two-family homes before a sale or change of occupancy.
  • For rentals, the township page notes state requirements for proof of liability insurance and a passed lead-based paint inspection certification on units built before 1978.
  • Landlords with tenants in place should ask the Housing office about landlord registration before they sell.

If the property relies on a well or septic system, the Housing page links to Gloucester County's well and septic information, and it also links to the county's online deed records, where you can confirm how your deed reads before the sale.

sections.h2: What fees and taxes apply when you sell in Washington Township?
sections.html:
The seller pays New Jersey's Realty Transfer Fee at deed recording. On a price of $350,000 or less, the schedule lists $2.00 per $500 on the first $150,000, $3.35 between $150,000 and $200,000, and $3.90 between $200,000 and $350,000. Senior citizens, blind or disabled persons and certain low- and moderate-income housing use a reduced table that starts at $0.50 per $500.

Each seller also signs a GIT/REP form with the deed. New Jersey residents use GIT/REP-3 and owe nothing up front, while an out-of-state seller may owe 2% of the price or 8.97% of the gain at closing. Your title company can tell you which form fits each owner on the deed.

sections.h2: How do tax appeals work in Washington Township?
sections.html:
Gloucester County is on the alternative assessment calendar, so the deadline to appeal is January 15, not April 1. File Form A-1 with the Gloucester County Board of Taxation, 1200 North Delsea Drive, Clayton, or call 856-307-6445. Assessments above $1,000,000 can go straight to the Tax Court.

The township's tax office takes payments online through the township site. Pay any open balance before closing so the title search comes back clean.

sections.h2: What quick-sale routes exist in Washington Township?
sections.html:
• Agent listing: more showings and the widest buyer pool, with mortgage approval and appraisal timelines.
  • Private sale: no commission, but you handle contracts, disclosures and township paperwork.
  • Cash offer: no lender, no appraisal contingency, and a buyer willing to take on repairs and the resale certificate.

Before choosing, list what you owe at closing: the remaining mortgage, any unpaid township tax, the seller's transfer fee and any repair credit the buyer asks for. Then compare the net amount from each route, and ask any buyer for proof of funds and a closing date in writing.

faqs.q: How fast can I sell a house in Washington Township, NJ?
faqs.a: A cash sale can close in a few weeks, while a listed sale usually takes longer because of showings, financing and the township resale inspection. Call the Housing office at 856-589-0520 to schedule the inspection early.

faqs.q: Is Washington Township in Gloucester County or somewhere else?
faqs.a: This page covers the Gloucester County township that includes Sewell, Turnersville and Grenloch. New Jersey has five townships named Washington, so check the county on your tax bill.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to appeal my assessment in Washington Township?
faqs.a: January 15, because Gloucester County uses the alternative calendar. File with the Gloucester County Board of Taxation in Clayton, or call 856-307-6445 for the forms.

faqs.q: Who pays the realty transfer fee on a Washington Township sale?
faqs.a: The seller does, when the deed is recorded. The fee table changes at $350,000, which is close to the Census median home value of $337,600 here.

faqs.q: Do I need smoke alarm upgrades before I sell in Washington Township?
faqs.a: Yes for one- and two-family homes, because state law requires 10-year sealed-battery smoke alarms before a sale. Ask the Housing office how the inspector wants to see it documented.
